skill.name: senior-architect

skill.summary: Plan software architecture, technology decisions, and project reviews with structured guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly documentation false positives from Markdown code fences and reference links. The only confirmed issues are local helper scripts that can write JSON output to a user-supplied path, which creates a limited arbitrary file overwrite risk if run carelessly.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts can overwrite any file path provided with --output.
remediation.suggestion: Write reports only under a dedicated output directory, refuse existing files unless an explicit overwrite flag is provided, or warn before replacing files.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can trigger static detections even when they are safe documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as documentation-only and avoid broad deployment commands unless the skill clearly explains review and confirmation steps.

content.value_statement: Architecture decisions are hard to compare across scalability, maintainability, and delivery risk. This skill gives Claude and Claude Code structured prompts, references, and local helper scripts for system design work.
actual_capabilities: Guides system architecture planning across frontend, backend, database, cloud, and mobile stacks.
Provides reference material for architecture patterns, workflows, and technology decisions.
Includes local Python scripts that validate a target path and produce basic JSON reports.
Helps compare trade-offs for performance, security, maintainability, and scalability.
Offers command examples for development, analysis, quality checks, and deployment workflows.
limitations: The included scripts are scaffold tools with placeholder analysis logic.
It does not generate real architecture diagrams without further implementation.
Technology recommendations still require project-specific context and human review.
Deployment commands are examples and should not be run against production without approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a new product architecture
use_cases.description: Create an initial system design, identify major components, and compare stack options before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review an existing codebase direction
use_cases.description: Assess architecture risks, dependency choices, and maintainability concerns before a major refactor.

use_cases.title: Prepare an architecture decision record
use_cases.description: Compare candidate technologies and produce a structured recommendation with trade-offs and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the current architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a codebase or product idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the senior-architect skill to describe the architecture of this project in simple terms. Include the main components, data flow, and likely risks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare technology choices
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose between frameworks, databases, or cloud services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the senior-architect skill to compare these options for my project: [options]. Evaluate scalability, maintainability, team fit, cost, and migration risk.

prompt_templates.title: Create a system design plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a feature or service before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the senior-architect skill to design a system for [feature]. Include components, APIs, data model, operational concerns, and key trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit architecture for scale
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before growth, migration, or launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the senior-architect skill to audit this architecture for scale and reliability. Identify bottlenecks, failure modes, observability gaps, and phased improvements.

output_examples.input: Design a multi-tenant SaaS dashboard for enterprise customers.
output: A component map covering web app, API layer, authorization, tenant data isolation, billing, and background jobs.
A trade-off section comparing shared database, separate schema, and separate database tenancy models.
A phased plan that starts with safe defaults and leaves room for larger enterprise isolation later.

output_examples.input: Compare Next.js with a separate React and Node.js stack.
output: A decision matrix for developer experience, deployment model, performance, routing complexity, and team ownership.
A recommendation based on product requirements and operational constraints.
Risks to revisit after traffic, team size, or compliance needs change.

output_examples.input: Review the architecture before a major refactor.
output: A short list of current coupling points and migration risks.
Suggested boundaries for services, modules, and data ownership.
A staged refactor path that avoids a large rewrite.

best_practices: Provide product goals, expected traffic, team size, and operational constraints before asking for recommendations.
Ask for explicit trade-offs instead of a single best technology choice.
Review generated plans with engineers who own production operations and security requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not run deployment or infrastructure commands from examples without reviewing the target environment.
Do not treat scaffold script output as a complete architecture audit.
Do not choose a technology stack without considering team experience and maintenance cost.

faq.question: Does this skill write production-ready architecture code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on planning, comparison, and lightweight analysis. Implementation still requires engineering review.

faq.question: Can it analyze an existing repository?
faq.answer: Yes, it includes helper scripts that accept a target path and produce basic reports. The script logic is mostly scaffolded.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the included scripts?
faq.answer: They run locally and do not use the network. Use care with the --output option because it can overwrite a chosen file.

faq.question: What architecture topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers system design, technology selection, performance, security, maintainability, cloud, mobile, frontend, backend, and databases.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for technical leads, senior developers, engineering managers, and teams preparing architecture decisions.
